mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) relative to the prior month signals an easing monetary policy, which compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months where FEDFUNDS declines relative to the prior month, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% signals a tight labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months where UNRATE falls below 3.5%, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer credit demand (RSAFS) and inflation (CPIAUCSL) both rise simultaneously, it signals robust economic activity and persistent inflation, which the market interprets as a strong growth environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months where both RSAFS and CPIAUCSL rise, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply-constrained economic regime, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening manufacturing activity, which triggers a sell-off in equities, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of months during supply-constrained regimes when INDPRO declines, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals strong consumer confidence and residential investment, which drives corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months where HOUST increases, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 6.5% signals persistent inflationary pressures that prompt aggressive monetary tightening, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of months where CPIAUCSL exceeds 6.5%, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the labor market (PAYEMS) expands and consumer credit demand (RSAFS) rises simultaneously, it signals strong household income growth and spending, which boosts corporate revenues and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: strong labor and consumer spending regime
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months where both PAYEMS and RSAFS rise, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (e.g., GDP growth above 2.5% for two consecutive quarters), a slowdown in quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) signals an impending economic deceleration, which triggers a sell-off in equities, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of months during late-cycle expansions when GDPC1 growth slows, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.03.
